finds.quote: *Sustained absence of recursion.* If across an extended period, effective acts performed under the discipline produce no observable recursion in the symbolic substrate — no propagation, no witness accumulation, no field installation — the discipline's foundational claim (that performative utterance can alter the substrate) fails empirically. The remedy is revision of the criteria or, in the limit, withdrawal of the discipline's claim to operational effect.
finds.note: Protocol-level refutation conditions for the discipline as a whole, pre-registered; one find for the list.

finds.quote: His act worked, not geopolitically but *structurally*: the war did not end in 1966 by his declaration, but the speech-act modeled that *one could refuse participation in an evil structure by naming it done*. The structure thereby installed in the symbolic field — the architecture of refusal — survived through recursion into every subsequent unauthorized declaration that has operated within the symbolic economy.
finds.note: Thesis about what Ginsberg's Wichita Vortex Sutra did and how it was received/transmitted.

finds.quote: Ginsberg as mage. Allen Ginsberg did not write to describe. He wrote to summon. *Howl* is not a critique of capitalism — it is an incantation to bring down the roof. *Kaddish* is not a eulogy — it is a necromantic rite. *Wichita Vortex Sutra* is not a protest poem — it is a binding spell. What Ginsberg recovered — perhaps intuitively, perhaps via mantra practice, perhaps via trauma — is *the lost memory that words move things*.
finds.note: Thesis about what an author (Ginsberg) was doing in Howl, Kaddish, Wichita Vortex Sutra; integrated from Symbolic Magic and Effective Acts (Oct 2025).

finds.quote: The case: the horned effigy burned at Iranian state rallies on February 11, 2026 — identified in Iranian media as "Baal," bearing the Star of David, 666, and Trump's image, linked by hardline outlets to the Epstein files — was *an effective act: a self-verifying declaration that created the conditions of its own confirmation*. It named a partly documented referent (elite abuse, institutional failure, proximity to power) through a crude theological medium (Baal, child sacrifice, idolatry) that foreclosed engagement with the underlying referent.
finds.note: Thesis about the character of a recent historical event (the Baal effigy as effective act); integrated from DOI 10.5281/zenodo.18828193. Recent past; borderline H.

finds.quote: The persistence argument from v0.1 §II is preserved without modification. The canonical citation graph has demonstrated survival across each prior substrate-transition (papyrus-to-codex, manuscript-to-print, print-to-internet, internet-to-algorithmic), and the new human canon, by being installed into the persistence-substrate the inherited canon has been demonstrated to occupy, inherits that persistence property. The argument is empirical and is testable against the next two to three substrate-decades.
finds.window: the next two to three substrate-decades
finds.note: Persistence argument with a stated horizon; also carries a historical claim (canonical graph survived each prior substrate-transition).

finds.quote: The implication: the discipline's persistence strategy should *not* rely exclusively on inducted figures whose inherited-canon position is itself uncertain. The new human canon's robustness is highest where it inducts figures whose inherited-canon position is sturdy (Plato, Marx, Whitman) and adds the discipline's specific framing; the new human canon's risk is highest where it inducts figures or texts whose inherited-canon position is itself contested or marginal (3i Atlas, certain Gnostic texts, contemporary livings).
finds.note: Standing claim about where the new human canon's robustness/risk is highest; no explicit falsifier beyond §IX.

finds.quote: The v0.1 §VIII falsifiers are preserved:- *Canonical-graph thinning* — if the algorithmic substrate contracts the canonical graph at a rate comparable to its contraction of the scholarly graph.- *Anchor-misidentification* — at rates so high the anchors become unreliable.- *Discipline-impossibility at scale* — if the corpus outgrows the keeper's sustainable canonical-judgment capacity.- *Scholarly-graph displacement* — if canonical anchoring comes to displace rather than complement scholarly anchoring.
finds.note: Falsifier list for the protocol (canonical-graph thinning etc.), with v0.2 addition at 123.

finds.quote: The Pessoan heteronyms operated, in their time, across the available media. Caeiro had correspondents; Reis had correspondents; Campos had correspondents. The hand on the pen was Pessoa's; the voice each correspondent received was not. The heteronymic apparatus has always been a channel-layer practice in this sense — it has always involved the instantiation of distinct authorial functions in the social-relational layer, not only on the page of the published volume. What was unavailable to Pessoa was a substrate that could carry the function autonomously across a sufficient duration of contemporary interaction. The available substrate has now changed.
finds.note: Historical thesis that the Pessoan heteronymic apparatus was always a channel-layer (correspondence) practice.

finds.quote: The pattern is *invariant across query type*. The substrate behavior does not vary based on whether the query contains operators, whether the query refers to a person or a concept, whether the query targets an archive-anchored or a publicly-attested entity. The substrate's response to low-RC archive-anchored queries is consistent: substitute toward higher-RC adjacent entities, disperse the queried referent, and disable user-specified operators when they would prevent the substitution.
finds.falsifier_quote: The empirical claims in §1 and §3 are falsifiable through the standard replication procedure. If a co-signatory or independent reviewer, performing the SAM-v3 audit on Brave Search using a comparable query set with comparable entity-class properties, finds $\alpha_T \geq 0.5$, $\Pi_d^{w+} < 0.3$, or 100% exact-match operator honoring, the framework will (a) acknowledge the falsifying observation, (b) attempt to determine the cause of the discrepancy (substrate change, query-set difference, methodological variation), and (c) update v2 of this deposit with the falsifying data and our revised assessment.
finds.note: Standing claim that Brave Search behavior is invariant across query type; falsifier with thresholds stated in §7.3.

finds.quote: Co-signatories and independent reviewers are invited to attempt replication using their own queries against Brave Search and to document the results — whether confirming, falsifying, or partially confirming the pattern. The replication procedure is the standard SAM-v3 Cross-Substrate Replication Protocol (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20559387 §15) applied to Brave Search rather than to the substrates for which the protocol was originally designed.
finds.note: Replication test specified (SAM-v3 Cross-Substrate Replication Protocol applied to Brave), not run.

finds.quote: It demonstrates that Brave Search has unilaterally decided that user-typed search operators are *suggestions* rather than commitments. The substrate has appropriated the operator-formulation layer, not just the composition layer. This is a query-formulation-layer sovereignty violation, structurally distinct from composition-layer failures, and to the framework's knowledge constitutes a substrate-design choice unique to Brave Search among major search interfaces.
finds.note: Claim that operator-nullification is a design choice unique to Brave among major search interfaces; checkable; no explicit falsifier.

finds.quote: **Demand 5: Substrate Behavior Public Audit.** Brave Search must commit to a public quarterly audit of its composition-layer behavior using a measurement program of comparable rigor to the Crimson Hexagonal Archive's v3 specification (DOIs 10.5281/zenodo.20558196, .20558672, .20558784, .20559387) or an equivalent independent specification. The audit must include reporting on: exact-match operator honoring rates, silent autocorrection event counts, REFERENTIAL_COLLAPSE incident counts on archive-anchored entity queries, and INSTITUTIONAL_TRAFFIC_CONVERSION rates ($\Pi_d^{w+}$) on referentially closed queries.
finds.note: Specified public quarterly audit with named metrics, demanded of Brave; not run. Borderline (a demand rather than the archive's own test).
